He brought them closer to Bryan, and the rough, uneven surfaces scraped against the oil-soaked fabric of his clothes, spreading the liquid over his skin.
"WAIT!
WAIT!
WAIT!"
Bryan kept screaming while trying to move his hands to crawl away so he could at least get away from the threat that was getting closer.
But his broken legs slowed him down, and all he could do was watch in fear as Rex put the rocks above him, the oil on his skin and clothes shining in the moonlight.
"PLEASE...!
I’M BEGGING YOU...!" Bryan begged, tears and snot running down his face as he begged for mercy.
"I WON’T TELL ANYONE!"
"I’LL LEAVE AETHELGARD FOR GOOD!"
Rex ignored the broken man’s desperate pleas.
He laughed cruelly as he struck the rocks together to ignite a fire beside Bryan, where the oil was pooled.
"Tell anyone in hell, heaven, or the afterlife..."
"...no one is safe from the Lustful Villain."
Flames erupted instantly, racing across the surface and enveloping Bryan’s body in a whirlwind of agony.
The fire consumed Bryan’s flesh, causing it to sizzle and pop, while the acrid smell of burning hair and skin permeated the air on the mountain.
He thrashed and writhed in agony, his clothes igniting in the flames.
The fabric melted, merging with his searing flesh.
"GAAAAAAAAAGGGGGHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!"
The pain was so bad it was like being in a white-hot hell that was going to take over his soul.
He could feel his skin blistering and cracking, and his body was shaking uncontrollably as the flames burned every inch of his exposed skin.
The heat was so bad that it stole his breath and burned his lungs with every ragged, painful gasp.
It was like being burned in hell.
Bryan could hear Rex’s cruel laughter and see his tormentor’s amused grin as he watched the flames dance and flicker, eating up the man.
He knew that his last moments would be spent in a fiery hell, a show for another man’s sick pleasure.
This only made the unimaginable pain in his body worse.
"Please..." Bryan choked out, his voice a garbled, unrecognizable rasp.
"Please kill me... just end this... mercifully..."
He could hardly speak because his throat was closing up and his lungs were burning with each hard breath.
His vision started to blur and darken at the edges, and his mind started to fade as the pain became too much to handle.
As Rex watched Bryan’s life slowly fade from his eyes, his laughter got louder and more mocking.
"With pleasure," he said with a cruel smile on his face.
"But not yet.
I want you to remember the horrible pain of not being able to please a woman as you take your last breaths."
"You deserve the hell you’ve earned by being a pathetic, limp-dicked loser."
Bryan felt his life force fading as the flames continued to eat him.
His heart rate slowed, and his breaths became shallow and weak.
He saw Marceline’s face in his last moments.
Her beautiful features twisted in ecstasy as Rex had fucked her, used her, and claimed her in ways Bryan never could.
He felt one last, bitter pang of despair when he realized he had lost her and had never really had her.
Bryan’s life slipped away with one last, rattling breath.
His body went limp and still among the dying embers.
Rex stood over him and looked down at the burned, unrecognizable body of the man that deserves the torture from him.
He felt a dark sense of satisfaction wash over him as he thought about how he had gotten the best revenge and punishment for Bryan’s failure as a man.
"Good shit..."

chapters.title: Chapter 256. I’m Such A F-Ing Genius To Plan All Of This! (Abusing Mechanics!)
paragraphs: The morning light filtered through the curtains of the private guest room at the Silver Rest, a morning that followed nights filled with productivity in every sense.
Rex had awakened before either of them, and of course, he didn’t need much sleep. Just one hour and a cup of coffee were enough to kickstart his productive day.
This pattern was characteristic of his behavior since arriving in this world, where the unique quality of his sleep allowed him to become fully alert before anyone else had started to wake.
As the sun rose, casting a warm glow across the landscape, Rex took a moment to appreciate the tranquility of the early morning.

He understood that soon the hustle and bustle of the day would commence, but for now, he enjoyed the quiet, mapping out his tasks and goals with a clarity that could only be found in those serene hours.
He lay on his back, aware of the ceiling above him and the familiar sensations of the room gradually coming into focus, just as they always did in the first thirty seconds of waking.
"Phew... last night was some good shit! Rex exhaled deeply, expressing his relief.
"My libido is already screaming this morning," Rex said, glancing down at his morning wood. "Looks like I won’t be easily satisfied during this two-week break from the academy."

Marceline was sleeping deeply and thoroughly on his right, like someone who had been through a big emotional event and was now able to really rest. Her breathing was slow and steady, like someone who didn’t have to be anywhere for a few hours.
"Ah yes... the second woman who’s carrying my unborn child," Rex said while caressing her tummy. "Still bloated..."

Rex also noticed Linda was asleep on his left side, which was a natural arrangement that had developed over the course of the night. She was sleeping deeply and comfortably, like cat-type demi-humans do, having apparently decided at some point during the night that Rex’s chest would make a wonderful pillow.
"I do remember sleeping on these massive jugs!" Rex gives a small slap on her chest. "They felt like pillows, but better!"
Even when he gave that slap, he had learned that her ears were fully relaxed, which was the cat-type equivalent of being completely unconscious.
He stared at the ceiling.

Then he looked around at the way things were set up, the two women next to him, the morning light coming through the curtains, and the general shape of everything that had happened in the last twelve hours.
"What the fuck am I waiting for now...?"
He stood up.

The movement required careful attention to avoid disturbing either of them, but having full telekinetic control over his immediate surroundings made that much simpler. He was halfway across the room when Linda shifted her head from his chest to the pillow. Neither she nor Marceline seemed to notice the change.
"Let’s go check some useful skills that I could get."
Rex went to the sink in the corner of the room, put his hands under the cold water, and looked at himself in the little mirror above it.
He looked like someone who was doing a normal morning checkup and was pleased with the results.
"Hell yeah, looking good, Rex Rexilion," Rex smirked. "You just made two women pregnant in this fantasy world."
"Wonder who’s next..." His mind raced with possibilities as he towel-dried his hands, contemplating the encounters that awaited him.
Each encounter represented a new opportunity, and he felt a thrill at the thought of the more sessions he would have with different women who were going to be the mothers of his children.
"It can’t be Lily and Diana because they’re still not that age to get pregnant... but they do have child-bearing hips." Rex held his chin. "Their mother is qualified..."
"...but I want to teach her a lesson first.
"Well, for now, let’s see how much energy I got because yesterday I really went all in to make the most of everything."
After he said that, the notifications came.
[CONFIRMED IMPREGNATION: MARCELINE BANCEY]
[EVENT THRESHOLD REACHED: MAXIMUM BOND + CONCEPTION]
[FREE SKILL SELECTION UNLOCKED — ONE USE]
[ADDITIONAL BONUS: +1000 ENERGY POINTS]
[LINDA LYSANDRA — MAXIMUM BOND ACHIEVED: 100/100]
[FIRST MAXIMUM BOND BONUS: +1000 ENERGY POINTS]
[THREESOME MULTIPLIER APPLIED: ×2 BASE ENCOUNTER ENERGY]
[SESSION ENERGY TOTAL: +2000 ENERGY POINTS]
[PSYCHOLOGICAL DOMINANCE EVENT — BRYAN BANCEY]
[SUSTAINED AUTHORITY DEMONSTRATION — ELIGIBLE FOR BONUS]
[BONUS AWARDED: +1000 ENERGY POINTS]
[TOTAL ENERGY ACQUIRED THIS SESSION: 6,000 POINTS]
[PREVIOUS BALANCE: 1,000 POINTS]
[CURRENT BALANCE: 7,000 POINTS]
Rex read the notifications twice, as was his usual practice when he had to handle numbers.
7,000 points, plus the option to select a skill at no cost.
"Oh my fucking lust..."
He stood at the sink and let the full weight of that sink in for about four seconds before laughing.

Not the polite or controlled laugh, but the genuine one that emerged when everything unfolded as intended, with no discrepancies between the plan and the outcome. The presence of that zero was the most amusing aspect.
"That’s the shit right there!" Rex’s laugh starts to get louder. "This must be some world-breaking records!"
He kept his laughter subdued so that neither woman in the other room could hear him. Pressing one hand against the edge of the washbasin, he allowed the moment to unfold.
"Seven fucking thousand," he said softly to himself. "From just one night."
He washed his face and looked in the mirror at someone who had just finished a full audit of their position and found that the balance was better than even their best guess.
"Lustia," he said to his own reflection, "you are a fucking genius."
"But nah... I’m the genius one right here to plan all those encounters!
"Making Marceline pregnant, speedrunning a new woman’s maximum bond, and doing a psychological dominance to a cuck!"
"AGGHH FUUUCCCKKK! I WANT TO DO MOREEEE!" Rex was overwhelmed with excitement about his achievement, unable to contain himself.
He spent the next thirty minutes in the bathroom, reviewing the catalog with the same level of focus he applied to making decisions that often worsened his situation.

With seven thousand points and the chance to choose any skill, it wasn’t a good time to make quick decisions. It required a thought process that began with his most pressing needs and expanded outward, rather than commencing with what appeared most impressive and progressing towards justification.
First, he opened the free skill selection.

The full catalog was there, with all the skills available, no matter how much they cost or what he needed to do to get them. He scrolled through it slowly, knowing that the free version of this choice was the one he would remember for a long time and that he didn’t want to look back on it with regret.
"I need to be wise on this one because I don’t have any woman I could impregnate again."
Then he saw Weapons Mastery—Full Potential.
He read it again, just like he had that morning from yesterday, when he found out that martial arts and weapons were two separate entries in what he had called an "absolute scam."
The scam had not become any less of a scam in the days that had passed.
What had changed was that he could now choose how to deal with it for free.
"Grrgghhh... fine," Rex said to the bathroom mirror, the system, and the organizational structure that had decided that unarmed combat and weapons were two separate fields. "You win this time."
"Need this just in case I want to fight with various weapons."
He chose it.
[WEAPONS MASTERY — FULL POTENTIAL]
[ACQUISITION COMPLETE]

[INCLUDES: BLADED WEAPONS (ALL SWORD STYLES, DAGGERS, SPEARS, POLEARMS), IMPACT WEAPONS (MACES, HAMMERS, CLUBS, AXES), RANGED WEAPONS (BOWS, CROSSBOWS, THROWN), DUAL WIELDING, DISARMING TECHNIQUES, IMPROVISED WEAPON OPTIMIZATION]
[MASTERY IS INSTINCTIVE — NO DRILLING REQUIRED. AVAILABLE IMMEDIATELY UPON ACQUISITION.]

The skill he acquired instantly made his body feel lighter and more agile, as though he had been training for years. He felt a surge of power flowing through him, igniting a will he had never experienced before.
"Alright, time to do some testing..."

Rex picked up the small ceramic cup from the edge of the basin, turned it in his hand, and threw it across the bathroom. He aimed for an angle that would have incapacitated a standing opponent’s dominant hand from a distance of twenty meters.

The throw exhibited the precision he had been seeking: it was as if a seasoned professional, with twenty years of experience, had mastered every superfluous motion. The release point, trajectory, and follow-through were all perfectly aligned to achieve a definitive result rather than merely an approximation.
He caught it with his left hand when it came back.
"That’s more like it," he said.
"With this I become even more OP!"

chapters.title: Chapter 257. I’ve Mastered Martial Arts, Weapons, and Elements! (I’m Getting More OP!)
paragraphs: He put the cup back and opened the catalog that had seven thousand points in it.

"Now I got to choose this wisely because seven thousand is a lot..." Rex said while already thinking of a good plan. "I need at least a skill that could provide me with becoming something reliable for Aethelgard and even the academy."

The free skill was already allocated. Now, the challenge was to determine how to spend the seven thousand points effectively, focusing on enhancing his existing abilities rather than simply adding new ones.
He scrolled down.

He eliminated the more obvious options: immortality, which he had aimed for weeks ago but had become less pressing due to the avatar creation; enhanced foresight, which would have increased his awareness but was already sufficient for most situations he had encountered; and teleportation’s full potential, which was intriguing but not the gap he needed to address.

"There are many skills that are too strong, but I don’t need them right now..." He thought quickly about the more subtle skills that could give him a strategic advantage. "Maybe a skill that made me more adaptable in different situations or one that helped him blend in with shadows would be better for him in the long run."
"Sounds lame though..."

"What I need is something that could make me a professional at this fantasy world!" He knew that honing his skills in negotiation and resource management would be vital when dealing with the complex social dynamics he faced.
The system provided a suggestion on his third try.
This was unusual. The system typically refrained from commenting on the selection process, simply providing him with the catalog and balance while allowing him to make his own choices.
[SUGGESTED ACQUISITION: ELEMENTAL MASTERY — FULL POTENTIAL]
[COST: 5,000 ENERGY POINTS]
[NOTE: SYNERGIZES WITH EXISTING ENERGY MANIPULATION AND EARTHEN DIVINE AUTHORITY]
Rex read the suggestion and then the whole thing.
[ELEMENTAL MASTERY — FULL POTENTIAL]
[GRANTS COMPLETE AND INSTINCTIVE COMMAND OVER ALL NATURAL ELEMENTS: FIRE, WATER, ICE, LIGHTNING, WIND, EARTH, AND THEIR COMPOUND FORMS (STEAM, PLASMA, MAGNETISM, CRYSTALLIZATION)]
[EACH ELEMENT OPERATES AT FULL POTENTIAL — NO CEILING, NO DEGRADATION OVER RANGE OR SUSTAINED USE]
[INTERACTION WITH ENERGY MANIPULATION: ELEMENTAL SIGNATURES CAN BE COPIED AND REPRODUCED WITHOUT REQUIRING TARGET CONTACT. THE EXISTING COPY MECHANISM EXTENDS TO ALL ELEMENTAL TYPES.]

[INTERACTION WITH EARTHEN DIVINE AUTHORITY: THE DIVINE LAYER IS AUGMENTED BY THE NATURAL LAYER — EARTH CONTROL BECOMES DUAL-LAYER, OPERATING AT BOTH PHYSICS-LEVEL AND DIVINE-LEVEL SIMULTANEOUSLY. GEOLOGICAL FORESIGHT RANGE EXTENDS FROM LOCAL TO REGIONAL.]
[PRACTICAL ASSESSMENT: THE BEARER BECOMES A FULL-SPECTRUM ELEMENTAL COMBATANT WITHOUT REQUIRING TARGET INTERACTION TO ACQUIRE ELEMENTAL ACCESS.]
Rex only read it once. Thereafter, he read the notes about the interaction.

The note about manipulating energy was the most important one. He could only copy an elemental signature by touching someone’s system or flow of magical energy, which was what he had done with the fire user in the market district and with Zeraphyra during the Undead Bringer fight.
It worked, but you had to be close and have a way to get in touch.
That mechanism became unnecessary once Elemental Mastery achieved its full potential. He would gain unrestricted access to every element without needing to rely on someone else to provide it.

The Earthen Divine Authority note added another layer. Dual operation meant that he would be using his earth control for two things at the same time: the detailed control of the elemental layer and the larger power of the sovereign layer.
This would make the earthen ability much stronger than either one alone.
Rex considered the cost: five thousand of his seven thousand points.
That left him with two thousand points remaining.

"Elemental mastery in this fantasy world full of magic could really help me become an expert..." Rex thought while pacing in circles. "That means there will be plenty of good opportunities for me to seize."
Rex then thought of one person from Starlight: Elizabeth. "If I master magic, I could probably get closer to that smoking hot woman."
"Before I deal with punishing Helena, I might as well try to pursue Elizabeth, since she could open up another path for me... especially since she’s my homeroom instructor."
"And then I can fully access the academy with her assistance once she’s fully invested in me."
"Yeah... good shit right there."
After considering his plan, he starts calculating what two thousand points meant for the operational budget. Two thousand was significant.
It equated to ten base encounters, or twenty if he managed the sessions effectively, which was sufficient to address situations requiring energy without depleting resources.
"Fuck it! Let’s just go!"
"All or nothing!"
He chose it.
[ELEMENTAL MASTERY — FULL POTENTIAL — ACQUIRED]
[CURRENT BALANCE: 2,000 ENERGY POINTS]
"Those two thousand points... I plan to save them for later, just in case I need them to execute my new plan."
The acquisition happened differently than the others. It wasn’t the swift and straightforward attainment of martial arts mastery or weapon skills.
Instead, this one unfolded in layers, resembling the process of adding components to an existing system rather than filling an empty space.

The fire came first, followed by the water, then the ice, lightning, wind, and, finally, the earth’s physical layer merged with the earth’s divine layer. This combination evoked a sensation he hadn’t experienced since the gauntlet integration back on the island.
Rex stood in the bathroom with his hands open at his sides and felt the full catalog of elemental access settle into his mind like a whole library coming to a room that had only a few shelves before.
"Oh yeah... I can see every structure of magical energy inside my mind and vision..." Rex stared at both of his arms. "I feel stronger..."
A small flame flickered in his left hand, unique to him—neither borrowed from another nor a remnant of a fading combat system. It was inherently his.
He stared at it.
"Now this..." Rex said, "...is not a scam."
He extinguished the fire and then gazed at the two women, who were still soundly asleep on the bed. "I might have to forgo the surprise she’s planning to share with the others about her pregnancy.
"Since I’ve already killed Bryan, I know that no one will care about him because he’s rarely home. Marceline will probably feel relieved."
Rex began to get dressed. "For now... I want to refocus on my real mission: raising the two girls from Apollo’s harem, Nerith and Mireya."
And then he stepped outside.
The street outside the Silver Rest in the morning exuded the atmosphere of a city still determining its identity during the reconstruction period.
The pedestrians carried a distinct energy: they were purposeful, focused, and noticeably more alert than usual, as if they were processing an event that had yet to reach its conclusion.
When Rex stepped outside, he found Aisella and Talyra sitting on the front bench of the inn.
’Oh hey... I didn’t know I would meet them here.’
’Well good... they could help me get close to Nerith and Mireya.’

This was no coincidence. Aisella and Talyra were the kind of people who meticulously planned their arrivals—a behavior Rex had noticed when they reached an unspoken agreement without needing to express it in words.
Aisella regarded him with a diagnostic gaze, holding it for four seconds before appearing satisfied with her assessment.
Talyra, with her archer’s precision, took two seconds to assess him from head to toe before reaching a conclusion.
"Oh my goodness, Rexy~!" Talyra said, "You’re looking in better shape today!"
"True." Rex agreed, "I’m in great shape."
"Hehehe," she said. "You probably have time to walk with us right now."

Rex appreciated that Talyra didn’t frame her request as a question. She had a unique way of expressing what she believed were obvious requests; instead of asking, she made them into statements, assuming both parties already understood the answer.
"Let’s go." Rex wrapped his arms around their shoulders.
Aisella and Talyra leaned against him, their faces bright with happy smiles.

The three of them settled into the comfortable pace that had developed since their arrival on the island. It was a rhythm shared by those who had spent three days in the field together, naturally attuning to each other’s speed without needing to discuss it.
The city around them was undergoing reconstruction. The cordoning off of the western district extended further than it had the previous day.

This indicated that Elizabeth’s engineering assessment had identified more structural issues than the initial evaluation, suggesting that the damage was more extensive than first thought and required immediate attention from the crews.
The crews worked with the organized urgency of those racing against the weather, needing to complete the assessments before anything changed.
Rex walked with Aisella on his left and Talyra on his right, observing the city as it underwent repairs.
"I bet today is going to be a great day with some twists~!"

[SUGGESTED ACQUISITION: ELEMENTAL MASTERY — FULL POTENTIAL]
[COST: 5,000 ENERGY POINTS]
[NOTE: SYNERGIZES WITH EXISTING ENERGY MANIPULATION AND EARTHEN DIVINE AUTHORITY]
Rex read the suggestion and then the whole thing.
[ELEMENTAL MASTERY — FULL POTENTIAL]
[GRANTS COMPLETE AND INSTINCTIVE COMMAND OVER ALL NATURAL ELEMENTS: FIRE, WATER, ICE, LIGHTNING, WIND, EARTH, AND THEIR COMPOUND FORMS (STEAM, PLASMA, MAGNETISM, CRYSTALLIZATION)]
[EACH ELEMENT OPERATES AT FULL POTENTIAL — NO CEILING, NO DEGRADATION OVER RANGE OR SUSTAINED USE]
[INTERACTION WITH ENERGY MANIPULATION: ELEMENTAL SIGNATURES CAN BE COPIED AND REPRODUCED WITHOUT REQUIRING TARGET CONTACT.
THE EXISTING COPY MECHANISM EXTENDS TO ALL ELEMENTAL TYPES.]
[INTERACTION WITH EARTHEN DIVINE AUTHORITY: THE DIVINE LAYER IS AUGMENTED BY THE NATURAL LAYER — EARTH CONTROL BECOMES DUAL-LAYER, OPERATING AT BOTH PHYSICS-LEVEL AND DIVINE-LEVEL SIMULTANEOUSLY.
GEOLOGICAL FORESIGHT RANGE EXTENDS FROM LOCAL TO REGIONAL.]
[PRACTICAL ASSESSMENT: THE BEARER BECOMES A FULL-SPECTRUM ELEMENTAL COMBATANT WITHOUT REQUIRING TARGET INTERACTION TO ACQUIRE ELEMENTAL ACCESS.]
Rex only read it once.
Thereafter, he read the notes about the interaction.
The note about manipulating energy was the most important one.

He could only copy an elemental signature by touching someone’s system or flow of magical energy, which was what he had done with the fire user in the market district and with Zeraphyra during the Undead Bringer fight.
It worked, but you had to be close and have a way to get in touch.
That mechanism became unnecessary once Elemental Mastery achieved its full potential.
He would gain unrestricted access to every element without needing to rely on someone else to provide it.
The Earthen Divine Authority note added another layer.
Dual operation meant that he would be using his earth control for two things at the same time: the detailed control of the elemental layer and the larger power of the sovereign layer.
This would make the earthen ability much stronger than either one alone.
Rex considered the cost: five thousand of his seven thousand points.
That left him with two thousand points remaining.
"Elemental mastery in this fantasy world full of magic could really help me become an expert..." Rex thought while pacing in circles.
"That means there will be plenty of good opportunities for me to seize."
Rex then thought of one person from Starlight: Elizabeth.
"If I master magic, I could probably get closer to that smoking hot woman."
"Before I deal with punishing Helena, I might as well try to pursue Elizabeth, since she could open up another path for me... especially since she’s my homeroom instructor."
"And then I can fully access the academy with her assistance once she’s fully invested in me."
"Yeah... good shit right there."
After considering his plan, he starts calculating what two thousand points meant for the operational budget.
Two thousand was significant.
It equated to ten base encounters, or twenty if he managed the sessions effectively, which was sufficient to address situations requiring energy without depleting resources.
"Fuck it!
Let’s just go!"
"All or nothing!"
He chose it.
[ELEMENTAL MASTERY — FULL POTENTIAL — ACQUIRED]
[CURRENT BALANCE: 2,000 ENERGY POINTS]
"Those two thousand points...
I plan to save them for later, just in case I need them to execute my new plan."
The acquisition happened differently than the others.
It wasn’t the swift and straightforward attainment of martial arts mastery or weapon skills.
Instead, this one unfolded in layers, resembling the process of adding components to an existing system rather than filling an empty space.
The fire came first, followed by the water, then the ice, lightning, wind, and, finally, the earth’s physical layer merged with the earth’s divine layer.
This combination evoked a sensation he hadn’t experienced since the gauntlet integration back on the island.
Rex stood in the bathroom with his hands open at his sides and felt the full catalog of elemental access settle into his mind like a whole library coming to a room that had only a few shelves before.
"Oh yeah...
I can see every structure of magical energy inside my mind and vision..." Rex stared at both of his arms.
"I feel stronger..."
A small flame flickered in his left hand, unique to him—neither borrowed from another nor a remnant of a fading combat system.
It was inherently his.
He stared at it.
"Now this..." Rex said, "...is not a scam."
He extinguished the fire and then gazed at the two women, who were still soundly asleep on the bed.
"I might have to forgo the surprise she’s planning to share with the others about her pregnancy.
"Since I’ve already killed Bryan, I know that no one will care about him because he’s rarely home.
Marceline will probably feel relieved."
Rex began to get dressed.
"For now...
I want to refocus on my real mission: raising the two girls from Apollo’s harem, Nerith and Mireya."
And then he stepped outside.
The street outside the Silver Rest in the morning exuded the atmosphere of a city still determining its identity during the reconstruction period.
The pedestrians carried a distinct energy: they were purposeful, focused, and noticeably more alert than usual, as if they were processing an event that had yet to reach its conclusion.
When Rex stepped outside, he found Aisella and Talyra sitting on the front bench of the inn.
’Oh hey...
I didn’t know I would meet them here.’
’Well good... they could help me get close to Nerith and Mireya.’
This was no coincidence.
Aisella and Talyra were the kind of people who meticulously planned their arrivals—a behavior Rex had noticed when they reached an unspoken agreement without needing to express it in words.
Aisella regarded him with a diagnostic gaze, holding it for four seconds before appearing satisfied with her assessment.
Talyra, with her archer’s precision, took two seconds to assess him from head to toe before reaching a conclusion.
"Oh my goodness, Rexy~!" Talyra said, "You’re looking in better shape today!"
"True." Rex agreed, "I’m in great shape."
"Hehehe," she said.
"You probably have time to walk with us right now."
Rex appreciated that Talyra didn’t frame her request as a question.
She had a unique way of expressing what she believed were obvious requests; instead of asking, she made them into statements, assuming both parties already understood the answer.
"Let’s go." Rex wrapped his arms around their shoulders.
Aisella and Talyra leaned against him, their faces bright with happy smiles.
The three of them settled into the comfortable pace that had developed since their arrival on the island.
It was a rhythm shared by those who had spent three days in the field together, naturally attuning to each other’s speed without needing to discuss it.
The city around them was undergoing reconstruction.
The cordoning off of the western district extended further than it had the previous day.

This indicated that Elizabeth’s engineering assessment had identified more structural issues than the initial evaluation, suggesting that the damage was more extensive than first thought and required immediate attention from the crews.
The crews worked with the organized urgency of those racing against the weather, needing to complete the assessments before anything changed.
Rex walked with Aisella on his left and Talyra on his right, observing the city as it underwent repairs.
"I bet today is going to be a great day with some twists~!"

chapters.title: Chapter 258. It Seems Like My Path To The Nightwings Has Been Opened! (Breaking Time!)
paragraphs: They had been walking for about twenty minutes, in a relaxed and easygoing manner, like people who weren’t headed anywhere specific but were moving in a direction that felt right. Then, a figure appeared at the intersection ahead of them.

Rex noticed her before Aisella and Talyra did, as the Foresight was always active. It provided very specific insights about a woman in her early fifties who moved through the street with the confidence of someone who knew exactly where she was going while also remaining aware of everything happening in her peripheral vision.
’That is...?’
’Oh... it’s her... it’s been a while since I saw her.’
’Elaris Morr Nightwing... Theo’s grandma.’
’Now that I’ve thought about it... I haven’t gotten a taste from any of those Nightwings.’
’Maybe she’s going to be an easy prey because of her teasing attitude.’

Rex noticed that Elaris Morr Nightwing moved in a particular way the first time he saw her. She moved like someone who had been honing her skills for years, making the actions fully integrated into her body rather than merely a task she performed.
’These Nightwings are known for their sneakiness, huh...?’
’No wonder they dressed like a literal assassin.’
Elaris noticed Rex and turned her gaze toward him.
When she saw Rex, her face radiated the same warmth she had shown earlier, accompanied by the unique amusement she reserved for moments that were more intriguing than usual.
She changed her course.
Aisella noticed first. Talyra caught on half a second later.
In a hushed tone, Talyra said, "Look, Rexy... it’s that bastard’s grandma... Elaris Morr Nightwing," as if she had just recognized something that would alter the course of their morning.
"Thank you, obvious archer; yes, I see her," Rex replied sarcastically.

Elaris approached them at a leisurely pace, as if she instinctively knew the perfect speed to maintain and never felt the need to hurry. She regarded Rex with the familiar expression she reserved solely for him.
"My, oh, my..." Elaris smiled with her eyes closed while resting her cheek on the back of her hand. "Fancy meeting you here..."
"Rex Rexilion," she said. "I was hoping to find you this morning instead of having to go to the inn for a formal visit."
"Well... Informal works for me," Rex said.
"I thought it would." She looked at Talyra and Aisella with the quick, warm look she gave everyone around her. "Good morning, younglings."
They returned the greeting, and Elaris returned her attention to Rex with the quality of someone for whom pleasantries were genuinely pleasant but were not the objective.

"I need to talk to you about the Nightwing family condition right now," she said. "Specifically about what might happen because of my grandson’s actions and what you might be willing to do about those consequences."
"Why should I know...?"
"Your grandson started it."
Elaris nodded slowly. "I know... that’s why my family’s reputation is in your hands... or more precisely, in your words.
"Forgiveness."

Rex finally sees the opportunity he has been waiting for since Theo punched him. Theo’s actions have significantly harmed the Nightwing family’s reputation, particularly since Rex has been hailed as a savior following the Apollo power explosion.
Some citizens of Aethelgard probably think Theo’s an asshole for punching Rex without any good reason at all.
’Oh yeah... this is it.’ Rex thought. ’My first step to invade the Nightwings... I’m going to have so much fun with this.’
"Forgiveness, huh...?" Rex said. "I’m listening."
She fell in step with them, making a comfortable four-person group that moved through the street like people who are talking and also going somewhere.
"Theo’s incident in the street," she said, "had effects that lasted long after it happened."
She spoke with the flat accuracy of someone who had carefully examined the situation, presenting the facts rather than their personal feelings about it.

"The public record of the event, combined with the incidents from two nights ago and the link between Theo’s behavior and the Nightwing household’s public image, has resulted in damage to the household’s reputation that extends beyond mere social embarrassment."
Rex didn’t say anything, which was the right thing to do because Elaris wasn’t done.
"There have been some problems recently," she said. "And not just once, but twice..."
"The household exterior has been vandalized on two occasions. Produce market vendors have declined to serve Nightwing staff for two days running."
"There was an egg-throwing incident yesterday morning that Iris and Aurelia handled without reporting it to anyone outside the household."
She paused just to sigh because she felt shame from Theo’s action.
"Thankfully..." She said, "My mother doesn’t know."
"She is on a long business trip away from Aethelgard and won’t be back for about two weeks. Iris and Aurelia have been taking care of things at home in her absence."
Rex took in this information with the same interest as someone who was updating a map.
"So that’s why you’re coming to me," he said. "Are you asking me to repair your family’s reputation by speaking to the citizens of Aethelgard?"

"You’re the person with the strongest public standing in this city right now," Elaris stated, applying her usual directness to the matter. "What you said in the western plaza two days ago is still being talked about in the market district."
"You were a good man, Rex Rexilion. Not only did you save the city, but you also helped people understand that Apollo wasn’t at fault for the explosion he caused."
"People who were in the northern district during the shockwave have been telling anyone who will listen about the direction you were walking in while everyone else was walking the other direction."
She stared at him.
"The Nightwing household’s situation would greatly improve if you publicly linked yourself to its recovery," she said.
"I am asking you to consider establishing that association."
Rex gazed down the street ahead of them. The morning light remained cheerful, indifferent to the serious conversation taking place below it.

He allowed the silence to linger for a few seconds. It wasn’t the quiet of someone contemplating; it was the stillness of someone who had already considered the matter, allowing the other person in the conversation to feel the full weight of the question before he responded.
"Honestly..." Rex said, "That’s a big thing you’re asking."
"Yes," Elaris said. "I’m aware of that...
"You do know that I also experienced public embarrassment when I got hit by him?" Rex made that comment to further aggravate the situation.
"That’s right! That guy attacks Rex for no reason at all!" Aisella chimed in. "You can’t expect him to just clear Nightwing’s reputation THAT easily!"
Then Talyra joined in, nodding vigorously. "True! True! What’s his issue have to do with Rexy’s relationship with Diana?!"
"It’s his fault that Diana has feelings for someone else because she waited long enough for him to confess!"
Elaris chuckled. "So it is true that my grandson is jealous because he cannot win over his childhood sweetheart..."
"Well, we all know it’s Diana’s choice to choose him," Elaris said, nodding. "And I’ve told my grandson that many times."
Elaris placed a hand on her chest. "But please, Rex... you have to help my family."
"I could help, but it’s not going to be free..." Rex said, not really asking. "What is the household offering in return for my humiliation by getting punched in public?"
’There it is... I fucking said it.’
’Now then, Elaris... what are you going to do about it?’
"I expect you to be the one who opens the path for me to start breaking the Nightwing’s woman!"

Elaris fixed him with a look reserved for those whose actions confirmed her opinions of them. It was the expression of someone who had been anticipating this question and was pleased it had finally arrived.
"I didn’t think you were the kind of person who did big favors without thinking about it," she said. "I was right."
"And for me... it’s reasonable."
"Yeah, so..." Rex asked, "What can the household give?"
Elaris thought about this for a moment, like someone who had thought about the question and was picking the best way to answer it.
"I can talk to my mother when she gets back." She said, "My influence in the household is not small, and Morwenna’s views on strategic alliances tend to be similar to mine."
She kept looking at him.
"So I hope you can come tomorrow night," she said. "We can talk about the details in a place that is more private than a street in the morning and the conversation can go wherever it needs to go."
Rex looked at her.

The way Elaris said that last sentence, the one about the conversation going wherever it needed to go, had a certain quality to it. It was the quality of someone who was okay with different meanings existing in the same sentence at the same time and who was watching to see which one he recognized.
Rex didn’t say anything directly to any of them, but he did acknowledge all of them by how he responded to the invitation.
"There’s one more thing," Elaris said, and her voice changed to a matter-of-fact tone. "Tomorrow morning, Aurelia will be coming to the Silver Rest."
Rex asked, "Aurelia...?"

"She has chosen to deal with the Nightwing household’s bad reputation in her own unique way by challenging the person whose reputation is most directly related to that reputation to a traditional contest."
"Traditional contest...?"

chapters.title: Chapter 259. The Problem’s Done with the GILF, and Then We Meet A MILF (New Problem?)
paragraphs: Talyra, who had been paying polite attention because she knew this conversation wasn’t hers to manage, made a small sound that was about forty percent a cough.
She indeed heard Aisella repeat the phrase "traditional contest" and began whispering to her that the Nightwings could be considered the strongest, surpassing any family, including the Starlights.

"Aethelgard respected the Nightwings because of their strength, pride, and dedication...! Making them the strongest and one of the most influential families in Aethelgard, especially due to their incredibly tumultuous history," Talyra whispered to Aisella.
Aisella nodded. "I heard... yes... but making the grandson’s problem into a traditional contest sounds kinda... off maybe..."
"A traditional contest, huh?" Rex said. "Sounds interesting, even though I didn’t have to prove anything here."
"I’m not in the wrong."
Elaris nodded. "I understand your point, but Aurelia is the strongest fighter in Aethelgard, and she’s likely to leverage her family’s reputation to pressure you into accepting it."
And that... is where Rex could see a better opportunity to at least teach Aurelia a lesson, just because she acted cold toward him when they first met.
"What does that even mean...?" Rex asked. "Forcing stuff at someone is not what you call being a good citizen."
"She’s betting all on this fight..."
"Heehhh... I see." Rex crossed his arms. "What’s the contest about?"
"Unarmed combat," Elaris said. "Traditional Nightwing challenge format."
"The winner of the engagement gets what they had agreed to ask for before the match."
"Aurelia’s plan is to ask you to publicly restore the Nightwing household’s standing if she wins."
Rex said, "And if I win."
"You would set the terms," Elaris said. "That’s how it should look."
She gave him a warm look of evaluation.
"I wanted you to have a day’s notice," she said, "because that seemed fair."
For a moment, Rex looked at her.
"That was nice of you," he said. "And I’m glad you’re being chill about it."
The corner of Elaris’s mouth twitched. "Well, honestly... it really is my grandson’s fault for being so emotional about everything."
"And of course, I’ll tell you more about Nightwing’s history and why this traditional contest is important."
"Tomorrow night." She said, "Come to the Nightwing’s household."

She glanced at him for a moment longer than necessary before altering her path and continuing down the street in the direction she had been heading. She moved slowly, as if she had accomplished what she set out to do and was now returning to the rest of her day.
Rex saw her leave and then thought. "That was a fucking INVITATION that I saw...
’Oh... I’m about to fucking enjoy this new path that leads to the destruction of the Nightwing’s family!’
’And when I win that contest... my terms are going to look innocent, but deep inside... it’s to punish Aurelia and break her bit... by bit...’
Suddenly, Rex spotted Theo about thirty meters beyond the intersection where Elaris had departed.
He was at the end of the next block on the street, in a spot where someone could see the conversation from a distance that was too far away to easily get to but close enough to see what it was about.
’Oh wow... what a fucking dick move for staying away from me just like that.’
When Rex looked at him, Theo’s body language changed in a way that showed he wasn’t expecting to be noticed and was now dealing with the fact that he had been.
He didn’t come near.

Rex studied Theo for about four seconds, enough time to grasp the situation. In that brief moment, he realized that Theo had chosen to send his grandmother to speak with him rather than approaching him directly.
Theo had chosen to remain an observer rather than engage as a participant. In this situation, he was more interested in watching events unfold than in understanding their implications.
Rex had met people in this world at different times who were cowards in the sense that they were willing to hurt others but not willing to take responsibility for what they did.
He felt a certain way about those people.
’Oh yeah... I’m going to fucking make him suffer just for that...’
’What an insolent son of a bitch who hides behind his grandma.’
’Just for that... I’ll be taking your grandma tomorrow.’
It was not anger. Anger was the reaction one would expect from the situation, but Rex had long since become immune to the emotional responses that such scenarios typically elicited.
The feeling he experienced was more nuanced than anger and far more patient. "Anyway... let’s return to the girls who likely wanted to enjoy their walk back."
He turned back to the street.
"Let’s keep walking," he said to Talyra and Aisella.
They kept walking.
"I know my man." Talyra walked next to him. "You saw him, right?"
"Yup," Rex said.
"He sent his grandmother," Talyra said, like someone who is just stating a fact without adding anything.
"He did," Rex said.
For a moment, Talyra was quiet, and then she spoke in the direct manner that Rex had come to appreciate, saying, "You’re not going to let that go?"
Rex said, "I will deal with it at the right time and in the right order."
Talyra thought about this. "Which is after tomorrow night.
"Yep, after tomorrow night, where he’s probably going to be there as well," Rex said again. "I’ll probably bring Diana too, just so that she can also confess her real feelings."

Aisella walked on Rex’s left during their conversation, remaining silent, which was her way of actively agreeing. She had a unique ability to use silence to convey information, achieving clarity equivalent to that of words while avoiding the imprecision that can sometimes accompany verbal communication.
And then... their peaceful morning continued.

’Goddamn... She’s so fucking hot...’
’This is a real milf... and what’s better is that she looks like a nun in my world, but I guess priestess is the right term for her.’
’Her body literally is for sins.’

Making them the strongest and one of the most influential families in Aethelgard, especially due to their incredibly tumultuous history," Talyra whispered to Aisella.

Elaris nodded.

I see." Rex crossed his arms.

"Aurelia’s plan is to ask you to publicly restore the Nightwing household’s standing if she wins."
Rex said, "And if I win."
"You would set the terms," Elaris said.
"That’s how it should look."
She gave him a warm look of evaluation.
"I wanted you to have a day’s notice," she said, "because that seemed fair."
For a moment, Rex looked at her.
"That was nice of you," he said.
"And I’m glad you’re being chill about it."
The corner of Elaris’s mouth twitched.
"Well, honestly... it really is my grandson’s fault for being so emotional about everything."
"And of course, I’ll tell you more about Nightwing’s history and why this traditional contest is important."
"Tomorrow night." She said, "Come to the Nightwing’s household."

He felt a certain way about those people.
’Oh yeah...
I’m going to fucking make him suffer just for that...’
’What an insolent son of a bitch who hides behind his grandma.’
’Just for that...
I’ll be taking your grandma tomorrow.’

chapters.title: Chapter 260. Apollo Has A Smoking Hot Mother! And She’s Thankful Of Me! (Jackpot!)
paragraphs: [AMELIA BRIGHTSOUL — DESIRE LEVEL: 0/100 — TARGET FOUND]
When Rex saw the notification, especially the name and the last name of the woman, he felt a sense of satisfaction. ’Holy fucking shit...’
’This is... Apollo’s mother...!’
’A fucking gem indeed!’
Rex regarded her with a gaze that conveyed his genuine interest, not wanting to mask his curiosity. This was a distinct way he communicated when encountering someone who captured his attention.
"I am." He said, "Even though you have an advantage over me, I don’t know your name."
"Oh, yeah, hehehe. I forgot to introduce myself."
"I’m Amelia Brightsoul," she said. "High Priestess of the Life-Affinity Temple here in Aethelgard."
She winked. "I’m also the mother of the one that destroyed half of the capital... Apollo."
Rex absorbed this revelation as if he had just discovered a puzzle’s missing piece, suddenly finding the fragments more compelling than they had seemed individually.
’Jackpot.’
"What about the mission, Mother Amelia?" Aisella asked.
"For now it’s done... and it’s faster than I thought because of the help of my dear husband."
’Husband, huh...? Good...’ Rex just faced another satisfying truth.
The mother of Apollo.
A High Priestess who had been away on a mission with her husband.
She went back to a city that had just been half destroyed by her son’s uncontrolled activation.
And what’s even better is that she had heard of Rex Rexilion, and her expression was unmistakable when she laid eyes on him.
"When I returned to Aethelgard, I heard some devastating news," Amelia said. "I also heard about your actions."

Her tone resembled that of a mother returning to find her son in a restricted area, her city partially in ruins, and an unfamiliar person in the street who seemed to be responsible for preventing the situation from worsening.
"What I could do," Rex said. It was the correct version, though it sounded like something someone lacking modesty would say.
Amelia looked at him for a moment with the judgment that a high priestess of any kind had developed over decades of judging people.
Then she said, "Honestly... I owe you more than a morning greeting can cover."
"My son almost gets punished hard, but you... you really saved him, and I feel so appreciated for what you did."
When she said that, Rex stifled a laugh, as he recognized another opportunity to undermine Apollo even further by having his grateful mother present.
She stared at Talyra and Aisella.

"Both of you are part of his assessment group, right?" she inquired. "He mentioned you in connection with the island, and Apollo said that Rex is indeed a good young man for having protected both of you."
"Yes," Talyra said. "And Rex is indeed one HELLA strong warrior and kind-hearted too.
Amelia chuckled. "Yep... I heard that a lot, getting praise by some citizens who got saved by him."
"Ahhh, fuck... the glazing made me want to laugh so fucking badly," Rex clenched his fists.
"I really want to talk more with my son’s savior, so please... walk with me for a moment," Amelia said.

This was the kind of invitation that people who were used to getting people to do what she wanted did not turn down. She did not have power over them, but she was the kind of company that people did not usually turn down.
"Sure, I would love that." Rex nodded.
They went for a walk.
[AMELIA BRIGHTSOUL— DESIRE LEVEL: 0 → 14/100]
As they walked, they discussed things that were comfortable for both of them. They had enough in common to keep the conversation going and enough differences to keep it captivating.

Amelia asked questions and listened to the answers with the full attention of someone who was doing it as a practice instead of as a courtesy. She found herself genuinely intrigued by his perspectives, as they revealed layers of his personality she had yet to discover.
Each exchange deepened their connection, making the mundane feel extraordinary.

She asked about the island assessment with the curiosity of someone who had sent her son’s friends into the field and was genuinely happy to hear that they had come back with results that were even better than what the academy expected.
Talyra said. "He literally saved both of us from a dungeon that was crumbling because we stole the gauntlets!"
"And he stopped a huge falling boulder that was about to crush us," Aisella added, emphasizing the gravity of the story.
"Oh my..." Amelia exclaimed, her hand pressed against her cheek in surprise as she listened to the story.

The conversation went smoothly as he discussed the problems they had and the creative ways they found to solve them. With each story, she could see how much he loved his assessment, which made her more excited about the project and what it could do.
"He cares more about our lives than that gauntlet... and what he did was truly... charming..." Aisella blushed as she recalled how Rex had left the gauntlet behind to save both of them.
Talyra nodded quickly. "He truly cares about those close to him, and he’ll do anything to save them. Maybe that’s why he stands for Apollo."
Amelia smiled as she closed her eyes. "So it’s true that Rex is a reliable guy."
She asked about the ambush of the capital, especially the northern district, the shockwave, and what Rex had seen during the defensive engagement.
Rex’s voice dropped, and his expression shifted as he recalled the intensity of that moment. He was clearly embellishing his story for dramatic effect.
"It was nothing like anything I’ve ever experienced." He said, "But that day taught us a great deal."
"I hate it when everyone starts blaming Apollo for his actions. It feels like they’re forgetting all that he did for the capital."
"That was really nice of you, Rex..." Amelia began to give affectionate touches without realizing it, such as resting her hand on his shoulder.
’Ah yeah... this is going to be easy.’

Rex gave Amelia more of the versions of events that were true and helpful and that made her think of him in a way that was very similar to the true picture, because the picture that was most helpful to Rex was also the one that was most consistent with the true account of what he had done.
It took them about six blocks of conversation before Amelia naturally said, "I would really like to continue this because I love hearing you say all of that!"
"Would you be willing to come to our house? Apollo is there and has asked to speak with you so he can express his gratitude."
Talyra looked at Rex in a way that made him feel positive instead of commenting.
When Rex looked at Aisella, she gave him the nod she used when she had thought about something and decided it was okay.
"I would love that," Rex said.
"Great~!"
[AMELIA BRIGHTSOUL — DESIRE LEVEL: 14 → 31/100]
Rex then gave a loot at both Aisella and Talyra to tell them that he’s going to go alone with Amelia.
Rex then looked at both Aisella and Talyra with a different look.
Talyra was the first to notice.
It wasn’t a word. It wasn’t even a gesture.
Rex’s eyes moved in a way that suggested he was conveying something without actually speaking. In just a split second, a sideways glance in their direction carried the weight of an entire sentence.
That look didn’t ask for or demand anything but somehow communicated everything all at once.
She pushed Aisella’s arm with her elbow.
Aisella got it right away.
Amelia glanced at both of them. "I assume you both wanted to join us to meet Apollo, right?"
They looked at each other for a moment, quietly and with the kind of understanding that only comes from having survived a dungeon that was falling apart together.
Aisella’s lips turned up, but only a little. Talyra pressed her lips together to keep a smile from getting too big.
"I’m sorry, Mother Amelia... but he’s going in alone."
"Eh? Why?" Amelia tilted her head.
"Actually—" Talyra said, her voice light and perfectly casual.
She turned to Amelia with the look of someone who had just remembered something crucial. "I totally forgot that I had something to do this afternoon."
Amelia blinked and looked at her. "Oh?"
Talyra went on, "The academy sent a follow-up notice about our assessment documentation," and the excuse came out so smoothly that even Rex almost believed her.
"I’ve been putting it off, and if I don’t do it soon, the administrative instructor will send me another letter like that."
Amelia chuckled quietly. "I know those letters very well, and Apollo has gotten a few of those himself."
"Yeah, see?" Talyra said with a smile.
Aisella quietly put her hands together in front of her. "I’m also going with her."
"We share most of the same documents." She bowed her head toward Amelia in a respectful way. "I hope you can forgive us for not joining."
"It was a real pleasure to meet you again, High Priestess."
Amelia shook her head in a friendly way. "Dear, it was all my pleasure."
"You are both wonderful, and I can see why Rex talks so highly of the people around him." She put one hand over her heart for a short time.
"Please, don’t let me stop you with your other schedule."

chapters.title: Chapter 261. Visiting Apollo’s House To Meet Him. (Nah, I’m Only After His Mother)
paragraphs: The goodbyes were warm and unhurried. Amelia clasped both of Talyra’s hands in hers, like older women do when they want someone to feel truly seen.
Talyra, known for her lack of sentimentality, refrained from making any sarcastic remarks, which spoke volumes in itself.
Talyra turned to Rex when Amelia stepped forward a little bit to give him a moment and adjusted the strap on the small bag she was carrying.
She didn’t say anything at all, but she did give him a look that said, "You owe me and don’t waste this."
Then she pointed two fingers at her own eyes and then back at him.
Rex turned his head. "What was that...?"
"Nothing," she said.
Then she smiled, and it was a real smile, not one that was fake. "Have fun being so dependable, Rexy~!"
Rex then realized that she’s being assisted by Talyra and Aisella.
’Oh my fucking lust... Talyra... you genius bitch, I didn’t know you really get what I want right now in this situation.’
Aisella walked up to her and looked at him again. She spoke in a quieter, more honest way, without any show.
"She’s a good person," Aisella said simply. "Be honest with her."
Rex looked at her for a moment. The way she said it made it sound like the sentence had more than one meaning.
"I always am," he said.
Aisella nodded once.
After that, they turned and walked together in the other direction, their footsteps fading into the sounds of Aethelgard’s streets as they recovered.
Rex watched them leave for exactly two seconds before turning back to Amelia.
She had waited patiently, like someone who was used to people needing a moment. Her hands were loosely clasped, and she was open and not bothered by the delay.
"Should we?" she asked.
"Yeah, let’s go." Rex walked next to her.

The Brightsoul household was located in the district next to the Academy grounds, specifically in a neighborhood where individuals with significant institutional positions lived without prioritizing the display of their status.

The house was big enough for a senior cleric to live in. It was well-kept and organized around the needs of people who worked in the life-affinity tradition, which included spaces for communal gatherings, private study, and areas for practicing their craft.
Amelia initiated another conversation, saying, "Judging by how close they are to you, I think Apollo really let them loose, huh?"
Rex didn’t expect her to say that, but he already knew the answer. "Well, Apollo didn’t really pay much attention to them.
"Yeah, I noticed... my son is indeed a dense young man who couldn’t express his feelings really well." Amelia chuckled. "And I don’t blame him or you at all."

"In fact, my son has been granted a system blessing known as the Harem King Protocol, although he hasn’t really made good use of it. At least he also has another blessing: divine favor from the goddess of life herself."

chapters.title: Chapter 262. Just Keep Talking About Apollo With Her (It’s Boring, but I Want Her!)
paragraphs: Amelia turned to Rex.
"I’m sorry... it looks he’s really in a tight situation right now."
"It’s okay," Rex said in a low voice. "Don’t push him too much."
The look she gave him at that moment was one he had been anticipating, reflecting the expression of someone whose trust in another person had shifted from provisional to more settled.
"I really am sorry," she said. "You came this far just to check on him."
"Don’t be sorry," Rex said. "He needs all the time he needs, and the rest will come when it does."
[AMELIA BRIGHTSOUL — DESIRE LEVEL: 31 → 47/100]
They left the hallway and went to the main sitting room. Amelia easily put the kettle on, as if she were someone who ran her house well and without fuss.

The sitting room now had the feel of the afternoon. The light had changed since they got there, and Rex realized they had been talking and walking for longer than the morning felt like it should have.
He sat down, and Amelia sat down across from him. The tea came, and the afternoon went on.
Before she spoke, she cradled her cup with both hands and let out a sigh. "Hahh..."
Then she said, "You know, he wasn’t always like this."
"He’s now closed off, with the door shut. That’s not who he was at first."
"Who did he start as?" Rex asked.

She talked about Apollo with the kind of love that comes from someone who isn’t performing it but just has it. The love manifested in specific ways, such as the actions Apollo took during his childhood and the moments she cherished, similar to how parents preserve memories that they want to last forever.
"He used to follow me into the garden just to point out the things he saw," she said. "Not to engage in conversation."
"He’d say that’s a wren or that stone is limestone, and then he would fall silent again. It was as if he needed to frame things before he could feel comfortable being near them."
"He really was a shy boy," Rex said.
"Terribly." She smiled, but it was the kind of smile that showed she was sad.

"He was the kind of shy that turned inward rather than outward. It was as if he built entire worlds in his mind." She touched her temple. "This made it difficult for him, particularly with other children. Especially with girls."
Rex set his cup down. "That must have been isolating."
"For a while." She stopped for a second and turned her cup in its saucer. "He eventually found ways to get around it."
"I believe that more people sought him out than he sought them. He possesses that quality—people are drawn to him, even when he doesn’t offer them much to grasp."

Rex was interested in this because it answered many questions he had, especially about the arrangement of Apollo’s harem, which was a group of women who all seemed to be truly devoted to him but weren’t in a clear romantic relationship that would have come naturally from their interactions.
"They love him," Rex said, his tone indicating uncertainty rather than posing a question.
"They do," Amelia said simply. "And he lets them."
"He just doesn’t always know what to do with it once it’s there."

The distance made sense because of the shyness. Apollo didn’t know how to bridge the gap between being cared for and caring back in the way that was needed, often feeling overwhelmed by the expectations of reciprocation in relationships.
Rex put this in the part of his mind that said "useful information for future reference" and kept listening.
"I used to worry I’d done something wrong," Amelia said after a moment. "When he was younger..."
"That I’d somehow taught him to receive love without learning to return it." She wasn’t looking for sympathy when she said it.
She was the kind of person who stated difficult things plainly, as if naming them kept them from getting larger than they were.
"You didn’t," Rex said.
She looked at him.
"Some people are built that way from the start," he said. "It isn’t made."

"It’s just the shape they come in, and they are the ones who feel everything deeply and have no idea what to do with the fact that other people feel things too." He paused. "It doesn’t mean he doesn’t love you back."
"It means he loves you in the only direction he currently knows how to aim it."
Amelia was quiet for a moment. Then she set her cup down with the careful motion of someone buying themselves a second to decide whether they were going to say the next thing or not.

"He told me once, when he was about fifteen, ’I know people care about me. I just can’t always tell if what I feel back is the same thing or just thanks.’" She let out a breath that wasn’t quite a laugh. "I didn’t know what to tell him, but I said, ’Thank you is a kind of love,’ and I hoped that would be enough."
"It was," Rex said. "More than enough."
"You can’t be sure of that."
"No," he said. "But I recognize the look of someone who is still trying to understand how to be worthy of the people around them."
"Apollo has that look, and it’s not indifference... it’s someone who believes the debt is too great to repay and hasn’t discovered how to stop counting yet."
Amelia was a good talker in the sense that she noticed things and told them correctly. It was nice to listen to her because it was always nice to listen to people who really paid attention.

But she was also, Rex noticed, someone who had been carrying this particular burden for a long time without anyone to share it with. Not because she lacked people around her, but because she was the type of person others turned to for support first, which meant there was rarely anyone available to support her when she needed it.

He engaged in the conversation as he always did when his contribution stood on its own rather than serving a greater purpose: by asking genuine questions, making precise observations, and listening in a way that ensured others felt valued and appreciated.
"Do you have people you talk to about him?" Rex asked. "Outside of this house."
She considered it honestly rather than quickly. "Not really."

"Most people who know him know him through me, which means that anything I say about him reflects on my parenting. And for those who don’t know him—" She paused. "It’s difficult to explain Apollo to someone who hasn’t met him."
"I’ve met him," Rex said.
She looked at him across the table with the expression of someone who had just remembered that was true.
"Well, yes, of course," she said quietly. "You have.
"Then you can tell me whatever you need to," he said. "I’ll keep up."

The look she gave him was subtle, yet it held significance. It resembled the expression of someone who had received something they hadn’t realized they were anticipating and were now thoughtfully weighing the decision to accept it or not.
She picked up her cup again.
"He used to leave notes under my door," she said. "When he didn’t know how to say something out loud."
"Little folded pieces of paper, and he still does it sometimes." She smiled into the tea. "I keep every one of them."
Rex remained silent; he understood it was unnecessary to respond.
That was another aspect of paying attention: recognizing when the most valuable response was to simply remain present.
[AMELIA BRIGHTSOUL — DESIRE LEVEL: 47 → 58/100]
’Oh yeah... this is working, even though I’m so fucking bored talking about him.’
The afternoon slipped into the night much like enjoyable conversations do: quicker than you remember.
Rex refilled her cup before she had a chance to ask. She noticed but chose not to comment on it, which spoke volumes in its own way.
"Can I ask you something," he said, "that might be harder than the ones before it?"
Amelia regarded him with the calm assurance of someone who had, over the past few hours, come to trust the person sitting across from her enough to agree to such a difficult question.
"Sure, go ahead."
"It’s about reincarnation," Rex said. He didn’t dress it up. "And I assume that you probably know what Apollo is."
"What he’s carried before this life, and what he’s been asked to carry in it." He watched her face. "How do you hold that? As his mother."

The question came across as he intended: not as an intrusion but as an acknowledgment. It was the realization that this thing was real and heavy and that someone was finally inquiring about its weight rather than how remarkable it was.
Amelia was quiet for a long moment. Outside, the first sound of wind moved through the upper branches.
"When I first found out," she said slowly, "I felt as if I had done something wrong by loving him the way I did. In an ordinary way. With an ordinary love."
She turned her cup once. "He was the Apostle of Life..."
"He had memories of other lives, other people, other losses. And I had been giving him warm meals and scolding him for leaving his books on the stairs."
"That’s not small," Rex said.
"It felt small."
"It wasn’t." He leaned forward slightly, elbows on the table, and his voice didn’t change in volume, but it changed in the way that voices change when someone means to be heard precisely.
"The apostle of life still has to live one."
"He still needs the meal and the scolding and the person who keeps his notes under her door." Rex paused. "The weight of what he is doesn’t make what you gave him less."
"It makes it more necessary. Someone had to love him as if he were just a boy. You were the only one capable of doing that."

In practice, it made him feel as though he woke up with a larger vocabulary than he had when he went to sleep. It was a familiar sensation of expanded access, yet without the disorientation typically associated with learning something new.
He could feel the rain that had fallen in the eastern streets’ drainage. He could tell that the stone on the lower floors was colder than the wood on the upper floors.
He could barely feel the specific geological signature that the Earthen Authority read as the foundation material of the Nightwing household, which was about four blocks away from where he was now.
He took note of everything and got dressed while thinking about last night’s encounter with Amelia.

"Not going to lie... last night, teasing a fucking priestess was the most fun I had," Rex laughed. "Her reaction was priceless, and she’s almost the same as his son when it comes to making decisions."
"I tease her hard enough that I think she’s probably going to sense longing for me, and I’ll let her get even more frustrated until she’s the one to ask me to do it again."
"Priestess or not... devotion to the Goddess of Life or not... I’m simply irresistible," Rex declared with pride.
When he opened the door to the guest room, the hallway was quiet. Apollo’s room was still closed, just like it had been the night before.
At the end of the hallway, where Amelia’s room was, there were sounds coming from someone who was waking up but hadn’t yet decided to be awake.
"It seems her husband is back, but I know she already cleaned up after that massive release from me."
Rex went down the stairs.
The Brightsoul family’s kitchen was designed for daily use, making it convenient for anyone who needed to prepare breakfast. He easily located the kettle and tea.
This efficiency was thanks to the Earthen Authority’s substrate mapping, a divine skill applied in interior spaces, which he appreciated more with each use.
"I’ve noticed that the power I received from the Earthen Apostle is heightening my sensitivity to my surroundings."
"Maybe I should start thinking about what new villain identity I should have come up with to create some chaos."
He was on his second cup when he heard footsteps on the stairs.

’Ah... there she is... the priestess who’s probably still feeling all frustrated, and I know that she’s going to act like everything is alright.’ Rex thought. ’Well, I do in fact love it when a woman tries to hide it...’
’Makes them so hopeless.’

Amelia walked into the kitchen with an air of slight embarrassment, as if she had not expected to find anyone else there and was adjusting her demeanor accordingly. She had clearly been awake for at least twenty minutes, evidenced by her styled hair and the clothes she wore, which signaled that she had a busy day ahead of her.
Her husband followed closely behind her, adjusting the outer layer of his temple robes in a manner that indicated he had performed this routine every morning for many years.
Amelia remarked, "You’re up early," her voice steady, indicating she had already resolved how the morning would unfold after last night’s encounter.
"Habit," Rex said. "The kettle is already hot if you want to make tea or coffee."
"Thank you," she said, and those two words had the morning’s special tone, the one that recognized more than just the kettle.
Rex, for once, acted like a gentleman by pouring hot water into two cups of coffee. He handed the cups to them and noticed that Amelia was trying to avoid making eye contact with him.
’Oh yeah... look at her...’ Rex noticed that her hands were positioned uncomfortably close to her crotch, as if she were trying to conceal something.

Her husband took the cup with a hurried thanks, and the three of them spent about fifteen minutes in the kitchen, conversing comfortably as if they didn’t need to prove anything to one another in the early morning.
Then her husband’s temple duties called him to the door, and the atmosphere in the kitchen shifted from that of three people to that of two.
"Apollo." Rex said, "Should I try again before I go?"
Amelia stared at him. "I heard him moving around before I came down."
"He was awake early this morning," she said, her concern evident.
"I could tell him you’re still here."
Rex thought about this. "Tell him I’ll be back when he’s ready to make sure that I don’t need to rush him."
She looked at him with a gaze that had been evolving throughout the night, one that had gone through several stages and was now calmer and more settled than any of the others.

It was as if she had finally found the clarity she needed, easing the tension that had existed between them. She leaned in closer, a soft smile crossing her lips, ready to bridge the gap that had kept them apart for far too long.
Rex noticed what she was about to do, but she managed to maintain the distance between them. "D-don’t worry..."
She continued, "I’ll tell him."
Rex set down his cup and stood up, appearing as if he had completed what he needed to do and was prepared to move on to the next task.
"Alright, I think I’ll take my leave now," Rex said, stretching both arms so Amelia could clearly see his muscles flex. "It’s best to let Apollo come out on his own and not force anything upon him.
"Y-You’re really leaving already...?" she asked, her tone revealing the longing Rex had hoped to inspire.

"Yeah, I’m busy today." Rex tries not to tease or seduce her today just to make her situation even worse, as he knows that leaving her with such feelings of longing will only add to her emotional turmoil. "I probably won’t come here for a while."
Amelia’s heart sank when he said that. She felt both disappointed and confused.
’N-No... I thought he’s going to stay a bit longer so that... we... we can...’
"But what if I need you?" she unintentionally whispered, her voice barely audible as it reached him.
"What was that?" Rex asked, even though he heard her clear.
"Uh, I mean... what if Apollo needs you?"
"Then just come to the Silver Rest inn, and if I’m not there... some of the innkeepers will probably tell me about it so that I can come back here."
"O-Okay..."
She then guided him toward the door leading outside.
He slowly walked back to the kitchen when Amelia said, "If the muscle soreness comes back," her tone making it clear she meant something more than her words suggested. "You know where to find me."
Rex turned around and looked at her.
"I do," he said.
She smiled in a way that suggested she was concealing something, her gaze unwavering. The morning light streaming through the kitchen window continued to cast a cheerful glow.
just as it had all morning.
[AMELIA BRIGHTSOUL — DESIRE LEVEL: 63 → 90/100]
Rex went outside in the morning.
’Heh... so close.’
’Well, I’ll save it for my next encounter, but today...’
’I need to at least get one of those Nightwings for some new experience.’
